key_insight: The paper introduces a fixed-point discrete neural sampler, Discrete Gibbs Iterative Neural Sampler, that reduces mode collapse and works on discrete unnormalized distributions without requiring training data.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable, amortized sampling and distribution transport for high-dimensional materials problems, including more accurate alloy phase diagram estimation.
method: Train a fixed-point neural sampler on density evaluations rather than samples.
Use a masked-diffusion-inspired Gibbs iterative process for discrete state updates.
Extend the framework to transport between pairs of distributions and different conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method scales to high-dimensional systems, substantially reduces mode collapse in practice, and supports accurate alloy phase diagram estimation.
watch_item: Performance and convergence likely depend on the quality of the fixed-point training setup and the chosen reference process, so implementation details may strongly affect stability.
paper_title: Fixed-point neural samplers on discrete spaces
